text:
maya: Heads up — noticed a recurring 95th+ latency spike on eu2-dedicated-2 when Tenant-B runs long-context batches. Other tenants on the same host get token tail latency.

simon: Oof. Any signs of PCIe errors or driver churn? node-level metrics?

maya: Nothing in dmesg obvious. GPU temps climb ~6-8C and CPU cstates creep up. Here's a quick topo and a tiny dmesg snippet: 

```
$ nvidia-smi topo --matrix
        GPU0 GPU1 CPU Affinity
GPU0     X   SYS  0-11
GPU1    SYS   X   12-23
```

[dmesg]: 
[    42.123456] nvlink: p2p peer access disabled between GPU0 and GPU1 due to link hotplug

kai: That matrix suggests GPUs live on different sockets/NUMA zones. If a tenant's job touches both GPUs (or the runtime migrates KV cache across sockets) we get cross-socket traffic and sudden PCIe/NIC contention. We changed packing rules last week to favor bin-packing across sockets for utilization — I think that's the regression.

julia: Can we short-circuit by enforcing socket-level affinity for long-seq jobs? e.g. a nodeSelector/taint like `gpu-numa=socket-0` and a scheduler predicate that forbids mixing sockets for pods with `long_context=true` label.

maya: +1. Quick test: schedule a long-context harness with `--gpu-affinity=socket` vs default and compare p95 across co-tenants.

simon: I can run that. Proposed command (runs loadgen from bench infra):
```
benchctl run --cluster eu2-dedicated-2 --profile long-context --placements 2 --affinity socket
```
I'll capture CPU/PCIe counters and p95.

opsbot: [alert] evict_policy:soft-triggered host=eu2-node-127 pool=dedicated-2 reason=thermal-throttle count=3

matt: If we enforce socket isolation for this class of workloads we lose packing density. Rough estimate: ~12-18% increase in GPU footprint for Dedicated. That materializes as higher committed capacity and $$$. We should compare that vs enabling transient burst capacity or migrating those tenants to a dedicated pool tier.

julia: Agreed. Two parallel mitigations: 1) Scheduler-level NUMA binding for labeled workloads, 2) short-term we can auto-migrate offending long-context jobs to a high-isolation pool (dedicated-high).

maya: Action items:
- simon: run the affinity vs default test and post p95/p99 + pci counters (ETA 2h)
- kai: prototype a scheduler predicate + taint label and a rollout PR (ETA EOD)
- matt: model the cost delta if 10% of long-context volume moves to high-isolation pool (ETA tomorrow)

simon: I'll post logs & graphs in this thread when done.

maya: Thanks — if tests confirm, we'll gate the change behind rollout flag and a canary on eu2. :thumbsup:
